events.title: Explain Echoes From Scratch
must_haves: One approximately 10-second vertical video includes intelligible English voice-over.
The narration explains that sound reflects off a surface and returns to the listener.
The visuals show sound traveling from a source to a surface and back toward the listener.
The explanation uses simple, child-friendly language and finishes without cutting off the narration.
The visual sound journey and the spoken explanation agree.

events.text: I’ll use colorful animation with sound waves bouncing off a distant wall, plus a friendly voice-over explaining what happens.

events.name: create_video_from_text
events.arguments: {"style":{"prompt":"Create a 10-second vertical educational explainer for kids. Bright playful 2D animation, clean colorful shapes, friendly cartoon character, cheerful inviting mood. One continuous wide view: a character stands far from a large rock wall in an open landscape. Show colorful curved sound-wave rings leaving the character, traveling across the gap to the wall, visibly reflecting off the wall, and returning to the character's ear. Make the outward and returning paths easy to follow, clearly demonstrating an echo as reflected sound, not sound produced by the wall. Gentle camera, simple uncluttered composition. No on-screen text or captions. AUDIO: A warm friendly off-screen narrator speaks clearly in English throughout the ten seconds, saying exactly: \"An echo is sound bouncing back! When you shout near a big wall, sound travels to it, bounces off, and comes back to your ears.\" The voice is a voice-over, not character dialogue. No music. Time the animation to match the explanation."},"end_seconds":10,"aspect_ratio":"9:16","model":"default","audio":true,"name":"Why We Hear Echoes — Kids Explainer"}
